Alex  thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps while the items are fresh: 

1) Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary use: customer support summarization + answer retrieval over proprietary docs (mix of S3 + internal DB).
- Traffic: pilot ~1000 reqs/day, latency target <350ms p50 for short responses.
- Security: must support VPC/private deployment for PII workloads; initial POC can run on Hosted with strict retention settings.

2) Immediate technical follow-ups (we'll help you land these):
- SDK quickstart (Python + TS) for local testing + sample app. Attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf.
- Auth: API-keys for hosted; for Private we'll provide KMS integration notes.
- Routing: suggest single-model canary, with fallback to a quantized cheaper variant.
- Structured output & tool calling: recommend starting with function-calling style JSON schema for extractors and then move to custom tool integrations if you need external actions.
- Embeddings/reranker plan: small index in Faiss for pilot; recommend 384-d embeddings and a lightweight reranker for top-10 candidates.

3) Proposed next steps / owners: 
- Tech deep-dive with your engs: book 60m to walk SDK, auth, embeddings flow (Action: Alex to propose times).
- Internal: Neha will own the integration checklist and run the sample app onboarding. Dev will be on the deep-dive for architecture and routing.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + sample code), integration-checklist.xlsx (POC checklist).

Helpful links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/redwood-sdk-quickstart 

If that all looks good I can schedule a technical deep-dive for Wed/Thu next week  what works for you?

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa  very helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- For the pilot index: we expect ~200k docs initially, updated weekly. Faiss sounds fine if reranker is lightweight.
- Latency: 350ms p50 is acceptable; our SLO is 500ms p95. Would love to see batching knobs and KV cache guidance.
- Security: we prefer starting on Hosted with strict data retention + contract clause; if the pilot goes well we'll move to Private.

I'll coordinate calendars with Priya for a Wed/Thu deep-dive  Wed 10/07 10 11am PT or Thu 10/08 2 3pm PT both work for our engineers.

- Python local server showing requests + streaming responses

Alex / team  hi, Neha from Solutions here. Quick note on what you'll find in the attached quickstart PDF and the Drive link: 

- Python quickstart: pip install redwood-sdk; example to run locally with REDWOOD_API_KEY set as env var. Sample app uses Flask and demonstrates streaming and structured JSON output (function-calling).
  Commands: 
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-xxxx
  pip install -r requirements.txt
  python sample_app/server.py

- TypeScript quickstart: npm install @redwood/inference; example Next.js API route for embeddings -> vector store -> rerank. Local dev: next dev; uses .env.local for API key.

- Auth notes: Hosted uses API keys; for higher security we support short-lived bearer tokens from our control plane and KMS for Private customers. We'll share a separate doc on KMS flow during the deep-dive.

- Routing & fallbacks: see section 4 in the quickstart PDF  explains model routing policies (latency-first vs cost-first) and automatic fallback to quantized variants.

I'll be happy to run the deep-dive and walk through the code. Dev, can you prep the sample Next.js repo link and a small script that builds a Faiss index from CSV?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Alex / team  adding a few concrete commands and notes for the tech deep-dive: 

- Embeddings + Faiss quickstart (Python):
  1) pip install redwood-sdk faiss-cpu pandas
  2) python scripts/build_faiss_index.py --input docs.csv --out idx.faiss --embed_model redwood-embedding-384
  3) python sample_app/search_local.py --index idx.faiss --query "refund policy"

- TS sample (Next.js) snippet for reranking: use @redwood/inference to embed and then call /rerank endpoint with top-k candidates. Include small server-side caching for embedding vectors.

- Local testing tips: run the sample app against the hosted sandbox with a test API key (we'll provide) and enable verbose logging to capture latency breakdowns. For batching tests use the scripts/load_test_batch.py we attached in the Drive link.

I pushed a skeleton sample Next.js repo to our internal Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/redwood-sdk-quickstart (see /samples/nextjs-rerank).

Happy to walk through this during the deep-dive. I'll bring the runbook for fallback policies and examples for structured tool-calls (function schema + validation).
